chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, and she said, 'I am pregnant, and I am your sister from breast-feeding, and I am not in a waiting period.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he has entered into her and consummated the marriage, he should not accept her word; but if he has not entered into her nor consummated the marriage, let him investigate and ask around, if he did not know her before that.'

key_terms.يُصَدِّقْهَا: He should accept her word/verify her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a wife claims she is pregnant and is your milk-sister?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the principle of 'presumption of validity' (istishab) is applied to the consummated marriage, where the husband must accept the wife's claim of pregnancy and nursing kinship unless proven false, reflecting the Shia legal emphasis on stability in marital bonds. For non-consummated unions, the burden of proof shifts, requiring investigation to ensure the marriage was not void from the outset due to the nursing relationship, highlighting the nuanced application of 'radāʿah' (nursing kinship) in determining mahram status.
